economics.labour-define2.0005.all: The price paid for labour (1), the amount a worker is paid per unit of time, e.g. per hour (1)

economics.labour-describe.0004.all: Raises pay of the lowest-paid (1), so improves their living standards / reduces exploitation and poverty (1)

economics.labour-diagram.0007.all: Supply of labour shifts right to S1; new wage W1 below We; new number employed Q1 above Qe; labelled.

economics.labour-evaluate-1.0006.all: Benefits: higher incomes, spending/multiplier, less poverty, motivation. Costs: unemployment in small retail/hospitality firms, higher prices, automation. Judgement: depends on how far above equilibrium 9% rise sets it and elasticity.

economics.labour-evaluate-2.0005.all: For: strike and bargaining power, 6,000 vacancies and emigration show shortage strengthening case. Against: government budget, public support, laws on union power. Judgement: shortage may be more important than union action.
